friction: Nothing was run in a browser here: the build (tsc -b && vite build) is green and a server render of the screen and of the dialog forms does not throw, and that is all the evidence there is for behaviour. What was hard: (1) Dropping files onto a list that is also dragged. DropZone's doc points `bare` at exactly "a list files are dropped onto", the skill points `useDragAndDrop` + `isFileDropItem` at GridList, and neither says that the two do not nest; I had to read React Aria's useDrop to learn the zone would be starved. One sentence in DropZone's doc ("around a GridList or Tree with dragAndDropHooks, take files in the hooks' onRootDrop and onItemDrop instead") would have settled it. (2) Card as a GridListItem's look has hover, focus, press and drag but no selected and no dropped-onto state, while ListItem has `isSelected`: a grid of selectable tiles is rebuilt by class each time. (3) A dialog with children loses `actions`, so every form dialog rewrites the button row; an `actions` that works beside children, or a doc line showing the form pattern, would help. (4) ContextMenu: its popover is inside its own area in React's tree, so a right click in the open menu re-enters the handler; and with `items` as a function there is no word on selecting the row that was right-clicked, which every file list needs. (5) SideSheet has no `classNames` for its content padding, and its standard form's 360px minimum is only in the styles. (6) The skill's Virtualizer row says sizes are pixels and the row's height is the kit row's, but the number (56 one line, 72 two) is in ListItem's doc, and nothing gives a tile size for GridLayout. (7) Under the Virtualizer the row's wrapper clips the kit's focus ring, drawn outside the row; found only by reading React Aria's VirtualizerItem. (8) No guidance on a tree pane that becomes a sheet at a phone's width: the app-shell block covers destinations only. What was easy: Tree with `items` and Collection, Breadcrumbs with `onAction`, the connected ButtonGroup as a view toggle, snackbar with Undo, and the first build passed type-checking without a wrong prop, which the doc comments earned.
